condition_other: cytotoxic brain oedema (OGD or glutamate in slices; acute water intoxication in vivo)
readout_other: Tissue water content; intracranial pressure; neurologic deficit score; survival; AQP4 immunohistochemistry and immunoblot
direction_notes: LIUS reduced brain water content and intracranial pressure and increased survival in the water-intoxication model, and reduced water content in OGD and glutamate slices when applied before the insult; no neural activity was measured.

target.label: hippocampal slices taken in 60 mm dishes

timing.protocol_description: Continuous-wave 1 MHz ultrasound at 30, 50, 100 or 200 mW/cm2 for 20 min, applied to slices in 60 mm culture dishes placed on the transducer probes, before or after (pre-US/post-US groups) oxygen-glucose deprivation or glutamate treatment.
Continuous-wave 1 MHz ultrasound at 50, 100 or 200 mW/cm2 for 10 min applied to the craniotomy site on the ipsilateral brain 10 min after intraperitoneal water injection.

source_quotes.exposures[1].fundamental_frequency_khz: was fixed at 1 MHz for all experiments
source_quotes.n_subjects: The rats in the WI + US group showed the increased survival (55%, n = 9)
source_quotes.sham_type: The unstimulated control groups were also placed on the transducer probes without applying the ultrasound.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: The rats were divided into three groups: (i) sham-control group (Sham) was subjected to craniotomy alone, (ii) WI group was administrated with water intraperitoneally to induce brain oedema, and (iii) LIUS-treated group (WI + US) was stimulated with LIUS on the ipsilateral brain 10 min after water injection.
